chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Regarding a mukatab who dies after having paid part of his contract, and he has a son from his bondwoman, he عليه السلام said: “If it was stipulated against him that if he became unable, then he would be a slave, his son would revert as a slave, as would the bondwoman. But if no such condition had been stipulated against him, then his son would pay what remained of his mukataba and inherit what remained.”

key_terms.عَجَزَ: he became unable to fulfill the payment obligation
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٌ: legally in the state of slavery or ownership
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: a slave under a contractual agreement of emancipation through payment
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: his manumission contract and its remaining financial obligation
key_terms.وَرِثَ: he inherited the remaining property or estate
key_terms.ٱشْتُرِطَ: it was stipulated as a contractual condition

ai.seo_question: What happens in Shi‘i fiqh if a mukatab dies before finishing his contract and leaves a son from his bondwoman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a mukatab who dies before completing his contract of manumission. The ruling depends on whether the contract included a condition that failure to complete payment would return him to slavery; if so, his son and bondwoman remain enslaved, and if not, the son completes the remaining payment and inherits the remainder.
